SongComments.SongComment: The first pattern features only the kick drum, just to give you an idea of how it sounds. The second pattern introduces the plain bass sample. The third pattern plays the same bass sample, but this time it's "ducked" by the kick drum from the first track. This is achieved by the following method:

The "Kick" track has a Signal Follower device attached to its DSP chain, which is tuned to the lower frequencies of the kick drum, using the LP Filter. The sensitivity was set to maximum, with very fast attack and release settings.

The Signal Follower is then linked to a Gainer device on the bass track, where it controls the Gain parameter within a range of -30db to 0db. When the kick is playing and has enough bottom end, the gain of the "Bass" channel will lower itself, making room for the kick.

In the fourth pattern, the kick is increasingly HP filtered over the course of pattern. If you look at the Gainer device as this is happening, you can see that the Signal Follower encounters less and less gain reduction over time, until the bass is almost completely untouched.
The final two patterns are present simply to fill out the demonstration.
